findings.detail: This is a root-cause analysis (RCA) investigation ticket. No code changes were made — the ticket's file_impact is empty and no_file_impact_reason explicitly states 'Read-only CI investigation; existing --durations logs and workflow/job history were sufficient, so no observability or production files changed.' The ticket status remains 'in_progress'. The RCA identifies root causes and proposes 7 remediation tickets (albinic-kyanite-goldeneye, coed-defectible-muskox, analogical-dashing-fennecfox, harmless-wavy-osprey, curricular-mean-cuckoo, despotic-dorsal-greatdane, classless-dainty-lamprey) but none of those fixes are implemented in this ticket. The Disposition section states 'Root cause confirmed. Remediation is decomposed into the seven linked tickets.' The 30–40 minute CI latency symptom has been diagnosed but not fixed; the defect still reproduces and the expected behavior (15–20 minute CI runs) does not yet hold.
findings.remediation: The 7 remediation tickets (albinic-kyanite-goldeneye, coed-defectible-muskox, analogical-dashing-fennecfox, harmless-wavy-osprey, curricular-mean-cuckoo, despotic-dorsal-greatdane, classless-dainty-lamprey) must be implemented and the CI latency must demonstrably return to the 15–20 minute range before this criterion can be marked met.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
